routes.label: Use an acute altitude and supplement sine reduction if needed
Convert the geometric mean into a side product

question: If the area of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(64\) square units and the geometric mean (mean proportional) between sides \(AB\) and \(AC\) is \(12\) inches, then \(\sin A\) is equal to:
solution:
First assume that the stated square units are square inches. Let \(b=AC\) and \(c=AB\), both measured in inches. The geometric mean condition says
\[
\sqrt{bc}=12,
\qquad bc=144.
\]
Thus we know the product of the two sides enclosing \(A\), even though their individual lengths are unknown.

To connect this product to the area, let \(h\) be the altitude from \(C\) to the line \(AB\). If \(A\) is acute, the right triangle at the altitude gives \(h=b\sin A\). If \(A\) is obtuse, the altitude meets the extension of \(AB\), and \(h=b\sin(180^\circ-A)=b\sin A\). If \(A=90^\circ\), then \(h=b=b\sin A\) as well. Therefore the base-times-height area formula gives, in every case,
\[
K=\frac12ch=\frac12bc\sin A.
\]
Under the square-inch assumption,
\[
64=\frac12(144)\sin A,
\qquad \sin A=\frac89.
\]
This gives choice D under that assumption.

The unspecified unit prevents an unconditional answer. If one square unit equals \(k\) square inches, then the same reasoning instead gives \(64k=72\sin A\), or \(\sin A=8k/9\). For example, \(k=1\) gives \(8/9\), whereas \(k=1/4\) gives \(2/9\). Both are attainable with \(AB=AC=12\) inches and an appropriate acute angle. Thus the displayed conditions do not determine one sine value unless the area unit is fixed.
